content.title: About
content.content: Meat‑free chow mein or chop suey without noodles is a vegetarian take on the classic Asian stir‑fry. Instead of wheat noodles it uses a mix of crisp vegetables, tofu and soy‑based sauce, delivering the familiar savory, ginger‑garlic flavor while staying completely plant‑based.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States as an adaptation of Chinese street food for Western palates.
Tofu, shiitake mushrooms and carrots provide a solid source of plant protein.
Traditional sweet‑chili sauce is often swapped for a lighter soy‑vinegar blend.
Skipping noodles lowers the glycemic index, making it friendlier for blood‑sugar control.
Some restaurants serve “chop suey” as a cold salad, letting the vegetables stay crunchy.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Tofu and mushrooms supply all essential amino acids needed for muscle repair and maintenance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Without noodles or meat the dish contains fewer calories than the traditional version.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Broccoli, carrots, bell peppers and other veggies promote healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Soy sauce and tofu provide vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Ginger and garlic have anti‑inflammatory effects and help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Tofu and soy sauce can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Regular soy sauce is salty; choose low‑sodium versions to keep salt intake in check.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: Some pre‑made sauces contain added MSG, which may cause headaches in certain people.

items.title: Iron absorption
items.content: Plant‑based iron from tofu is less bioavailable than heme iron; pair the dish with vitamin C for better absorption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stir‑fry hot, straight from the wok, in a deep bowl. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a squeeze of lime, or toasted sesame seeds for extra flavor. Tofu can be swapped for tempeh or beans if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store vegetables separately to avoid sogginess. Reheat gently and add a splash of soy sauce to revive the taste.
